studies.label: Field experiment: ChatGPT access in a Chinese technology consulting firm
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Randomization was individual, not by supervisor or department. Table 2 reports independent-samples t tests. The multilevel analyses use employee scores nested within supervisors within departments (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Results); these organizational levels are not randomized clusters. The main table prints intercept variance components for the upper levels, but does not name a robust or cluster-sandwich SE estimator (PDF p. 10, printed p. 9, Table 3).

arms.name: LLM assistance
arms.description: Employees received personal ChatGPT accounts through the firm’s API-based interface and usage examples, with instructions not to share accounts or discuss them with others. Workplace usage was confirmed by self-reports and account logs (PDF pp. 5–6, printed pp. 4–5, Method).

arms.name: Control (no LLM assistance)
arms.description: No LLM assistance; no control employee reported ChatGPT use (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Experimental Conditions and Manipulation Checks).

studies.task: Employees generated detailed written suggestions for protecting employee privacy when companies use digital devices, in an endpoint survey following assignment to ChatGPT workplace access or no LLM assistance.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT through the firm’s OpenAI API-based interface; underlying model version not stated

estimates.notes: Task-specific AI availability is not stated. The paper describes workplace account use and a response in the endpoint survey, but gives no AI-use instructions or account-withdrawal information for that response. question and outcome_with_ai remain null, as in the reconciled screening form; these are provisional numerical records pending with_ai versus after_ai classification and must not enter a question-specific synthesis until resolved. The survey measures the intervention endpoint, with no documented later retention test. The analysis uses one response score per employee; separate rater scores are not treated as independent people. Arm-specific participant counts are not printed and are not inferred from the rounded condition mean. The external raters are human, but their qualifications and the way their scores were combined are not stated. Table 2 reports independent-samples t-test p values, arm means and employee-level SDs, and Cohen’s d. The test type is printed, but the t statistic and degrees of freedom are not; both remain null. The paper does not define the d standardizer. No difference, standard error, or confidence interval was calculated. Source quotes reproduce complete rows; the locator identifies the relevant outcome columns, and the quotes preserve the printed decimal precision. Figure 2 (PDF p. 9, printed p. 8) has standard-error bars without numeric labels, so no arm SE is transcribed. The condition-correlation record is another summary of this same outcome and contrast, not independent evidence. Table 3 models are excluded because they adjust for variables measured after assignment.

not_extracted.what: Cognitive job resources, including the overall scale and item-level analyses

Self-reported moderator, not an output-based creativity or diversity measure (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Mediator and Moderator).

not_extracted.what: Creative self-efficacy, intrinsic motivation, job insecurity, and heuristic-task-characteristic measures
not_extracted.reason: Attitudinal, motivational, and job-characteristic control measures rather than scored creative output. Attitudinal and motivational measures were collected after assignment in the second survey (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Participants and Procedure and Controls).

not_extracted.what: ChatGPT usage and usage-frequency reports and account logs
not_extracted.reason: Manipulation and compliance checks, not creativity or diversity scored on output (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Experimental Conditions and Manipulation Checks).

not_extracted.what: S1-O2: Adjusted novelty effects in Table 3 Models 3, 6, and 10
not_extracted.reason: These models adjust for postassignment attitudinal/motivational variables; the latter models also include a post-treatment mediator and, for the interaction model, moderation terms. They do not meet the extraction rule excluding effects adjusted for post-treatment variables (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Participants and Procedure and Controls; PDF p. 10, printed p. 9, Table 3). The unadjusted Table 2 contrast is retained.

not_extracted.what: S1-O3: Adjusted usefulness effects in Table 3 Models 4, 7, and 11
not_extracted.reason: These models adjust for postassignment attitudinal/motivational variables; the latter models also include a post-treatment mediator and, for the interaction model, moderation terms. They are excluded under the post-treatment-adjustment rule (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Participants and Procedure and Controls; PDF p. 10, printed p. 9, Table 3). Both available no-controls analyses are retained separately.

not_extracted.what: Mediation and moderated-mediation effects for creativity, novelty, and usefulness
not_extracted.reason: Indirect and conditional indirect effects through cognitive job resources, rather than eligible full-sample randomized-arm total effects (PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, H3 and H5 results; PDF p. 10, printed p. 9, Table 3).

not_extracted.what: Interactions, simple slopes, conditional effects, and regions of significance involving metacognitive strategies
not_extracted.reason: Moderation and conditional/subgroup analyses are outside extraction scope (PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, H4 and H5; PDF p. 10, printed p. 9, Table 3; PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, Figures 3 and 4).

not_extracted.what: Additional no-controls multilevel novelty statistics referenced only in the unavailable supplement
not_extracted.reason: The main-text footnote describes consistent effects but does not provide an outcome-specific novelty coefficient, SE, or exact p value for the no-controls multilevel model. No values are inferred from its range of p values or substituted from the ineligible adjusted model. The full-sample novelty contrast is already retained from Table 2 (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, footnote 2; PDF p. 8, printed p. 7, Table 2).

not_extracted.what: Pooled-sample descriptive means/SDs and correlations among creativity measures, mediators, and moderators
not_extracted.reason: These describe the combined sample or associations between measured variables, not additional randomized-arm contrasts. They are not arm-specific means/SDs. The correlations with randomized LLM condition itself are extracted separately (PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, Table 1; PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Dependent Variable: Creativity).

open_items: AI availability during the privacy-protection response is not printed. Task instructions or access records are needed to choose with_ai versus after_ai. All retained records intentionally have null question and outcome_with_ai; they remain outside question-specific synthesis until this is resolved.
Randomized and analyzed counts for each arm are not printed. Total employee counts are confirmed; no equal split is inferred from the rounded condition-indicator mean.
External-rater qualifications and the score-aggregation method are not stated. Human scoring is confirmed, but the human_raters versus expert_raters subtype remains null.

The separate supplement is absent from the supplied PDF and the local supplement manifest lists no files. Requests to its DOI and the Crossref API fallback both failed with socket-access-denied errors. The supplement is needed for exact no-controls novelty multilevel statistics, fuller model/SE details, and the inconsistent references to Supplemental Table S5 Model 4 versus Supplemental Materials S4.

The paper does not define the standardizer for its Cohen’s d values. Table 2 does not print t statistics, degrees of freedom, numerical arm SEs, or confidence intervals; Figure 2 has unlabeled SE bars. These values remain null.
The underlying ChatGPT model version is not specified. The tool year is the ChatGPT product launch year stated in the paper, not an inferred release year for an underlying model.
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-11. Read the extraction specification and codebook first, then the candidate, retrieval, screening and citation records, both independent extractions, and their comparison file. Read the complete markdown conversion, including all references and editorial history. The saved PDF has no appended appendix or supplement and no embedded attachment. Checked every cited results page using PyMuPDF text extraction. find_tables() did not recover the rotated results tables, so their complete extracted text and column order were checked directly. The supplied comparison file reports only the additional condition-correlation records in B. Direct comparison also found differently named slugs and the t-test-object difference, which are resolved below. Retain the condition correlations because they relate randomized assignment to scored participant output; they are alternative summaries of the same arm contrasts, not additional independent evidence. Every screening outcome is represented by retained provisional records or a named not_extracted entry. No numerical analysis absent from both extractors was confirmed in the available paper. The supervisor scale is general employee performance, not scoring of an identified output. All Table 3 output models include post-treatment controls; they remain excluded even when they do not include the named cognitive-resource mediator. The counts, question, construct, unit, direction, AI availability, and within-person status were independently checked despite agreement. The final sample precedes random assignment in the procedure, supporting n_randomized; the analysis text and table notes confirm n_analyzed. No postassignment exclusions are reported, and arm-specific counts are unreported. The scored task is idea_generation because employees supplied privacy-protection suggestions. No shared sample with another paper is stated. No across-person diversity measure or documented AI-removal follow-up is reported; long-term dependence is discussed as future research (PDF pp. 11–12, printed pp. 10–11). The supplement was sought in the local manifest and with Python urllib using User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 at https://doi.org/10.1037/apl0001296.supp and https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1037%2Fapl0001296.supp; both requests failed with WinError 10013. Only the saved main article supplies empirical values. No effect, count, difference, standard error, or interval was computed, and no figure value was estimated. Source quotes retain the original text, including ligatures, with whitespace normalized. The reconciliation summary counts n_added as estimates absent from both input extractions; retaining B-only estimates does not increase that count.

AI was therefore available when the scored response was written: with_ai, measuring access to AI rather than its use for this answer.
